label: build:hud
mission: NFS-inspired DOM/CSS + canvas HUD: tachometer with redline and shift light, digital speed and gear, nitro bar, position/lap/timers, rotating minimap, center flashes, countdown, title menu, pause, results screen.

structured_report.summary:
Wrote the full HUD and menus (CONTRACTS.md section 10), replacing the stub. Every contract function is in place with the exact names and arguments. It is tested in the bench page and wired into the real game: a full run of menu, Enter, countdown, race, Esc pause, finish, results and Enter to race again worked.

Look and layout:
- Style is NFS Heat/Unbound-like: Barlow Condensed (bold italic, used for numbers and labels) and Russo One (logo and big numbers), loaded from a Google Fonts link that hud.js adds at createHUD. If the fonts can't load it falls back to DIN Condensed or Arial Narrow.
- Panels are skewed parallelograms with neon cyan #00e5ff accents, red/magenta highlights and dark glass backgrounds.
- Everything scales with the window: the root font size is clamp(8px, 1.48vmin, 28px) and all other sizes are in em.

Race HUD:
- **Tachometer (bottom-right, canvas):** 0–9 ×1000 dial with LED-segment rev band (blue → cyan → white → red), red-line zone, ticks and numbers. Glowing red needle with smoothing, so rev-limiter bounce still shows. Shift light: the band and gear box flash red near the red line. Big speed number and gear (R/N/1–6) in the middle; the gear pops when it changes. The nitro bar is a segmented arc around the left side of the dial: it pulses and glows when nitro is active and the segments go dim when empty. Two cached background layers plus a few strokes per frame; the redraw is skipped when nothing visibly moved.
- **Top-left:** big position number (gold when 1st; flashes green or red when you gain or lose a place), "/5", LAP 2/3 (red on the final lap). Below it: current lap, total and best times (m:ss.mmm), and a LAST row that appears after lap 1 with the difference to your previous best.
- **Minimap (bottom-left, canvas):** turns with the car so you always point up, with the arrow a little below centre so you see more road ahead. Track drawn as a dark outline plus a thin neon line, chequered start/finish line, rivals as dots in their livery colour (pushed to the edge when out of range), a grid that moves with the car, an N marker, and zoom-out at speed. Rounded-square glass panel.
- **Centre messages:** at most two stacked, the rest queued. Info is cyan, warn is red and pulsing (e.g. WRONG WAY), good is green. Text like "NEW BEST LAP 0:58.231" is split into a headline and a time line. Repeating the same message extends it instead of stacking it.
- **Drift:** a live chain counter (score, ×multiplier, bar) and gold "+1,250 DRIFT" pop-ups.
- **Countdown:** three start lights (red, red, red, then all green), huge numbers that punch in with scale and blur while the previous one zooms out, an expanding ring, and a neon-green GO! with speed lines.

Menus:
- **Title menu:** sits over the live 3D scene with dark edges and an open centre. Stylised logo (white-to-cyan "APEX" with a magenta offset, a recurring light glint, animated speed lines, red/magenta bar), the subtitle, info chips (laps, racers, night, rain), a START RACE button with a light sweep, and a blinking PRESS ENTER TO RACE. On the right: an event card that draws the real circuit layout with length, laps, racers and conditions, and a controls card with key caps plus "gamepad supported". Elements animate in one after another.
- **Pause:** blurred backdrop, Resume / Restart race, ↑/↓ and Enter.
- **Results:** finishing table with skewed rows animating in. Columns: position (gold/silver/bronze), livery colour chip and name, total time, gap to the winner, best lap (fastest lap overall marked in magenta). Your row is highlighted, with a big "YOU FINISHED 2ND" / VICTORY heading, PRESS ENTER TO RACE AGAIN and a button.

Bench page (dev/hud.html):
- A painted neon-city background with rain, the player car's tail-light bar, and a simulated race (rpm through the gears, nitro, position changes, laps, drifts, rivals moving on the real circuit, falling back to a demo loop).
- URL options: ?screen=flow|menu|race|countdown|pause|results, &cd=3|2|1|GO, &t= (freeze the sim at that many seconds), &msg=1|warn, &drift=1, &track=demo, &bg=0.
- window.hud and window.sim are exposed for testing.
structured_report.contract_notes:
Every contract name and argument is unchanged. Optional additions and the interpretation choices the integrator should know about:

1. **createHUD options:** also accepts `autoDrift` (default true) and `onSound(kind)` for UI sounds (`'hover'` / `'select'`).
2. **Extra HUD methods:** `confirm()` activates the visible menu's main button (useful for gamepads), `setSoundHandler(fn)` (the core already calls it), `driftPopup(points, label)`, `clearMessages()`, `dispose()`, and a `root` field. hud.js also exports `fmtTime` and `ordinal`.
3. **setTrack(polyline, opts?):** `opts.start = [x, z]` is optional. Without it the start/finish line goes at polyline[0], which is correct because the track's getMinimapPolyline starts at s = 0 = startS. Track length for the menu card is measured from the polyline.
4. **showMenu also accepts `laps` and `racers`** (the core passes them); otherwise it uses the config values. The menu fades itself out as soon as onStart fires, and onStart fires only once per showMenu (Enter, NumpadEnter, click, or gamepad A/Start). hideMenu is still safe to call.
5. **Input timing:** each screen ignores input for 260 ms after it appears (results: about 760 ms) so a held Enter or gamepad A can't skip through. Enter on pause therefore waits more than 250 ms, longer than the core's own resume guard.
6. **Keys:** the HUD listens on window keydown and never calls preventDefault or stopPropagation. It ignores key repeat. It handles Enter in all three screens, and ↑/↓/W/S in pause only. It does NOT handle Esc; the core owns pause toggling. Buttons can't take keyboard focus, so Space (handbrake) can never click them.
7. **Gamepad:** the HUD polls gamepads only while a menu, pause or results screen is visible (A/Start = confirm, d-pad or stick = pause selection). It only reacts to new presses, so a button already held when the screen opens is ignored.
8. **Pause and results callbacks:** after calling onResume, onRestart or onStart, the HUD hides its own screen (showPause(false) and hideResults() from the core are harmless). Each callback fires at most once per time the screen is shown.
9. **state.drift:** if it is an object `{active, score, multiplier}` (what the core sends), the HUD shows the live chain and pops the banked score when `active` goes false. If it is a number from 0 to 1 (physics drift intensity), the HUD scores drifts itself. If flash() is ever called with text containing "DRIFT" and a number, it shows as a drift pop-up and the HUD's own drift scoring turns off to avoid doubles.
10. **Extra state fields the HUD uses:**
   - `wrongWay: true` keeps WRONG WAY on screen continuously instead of blinking between the core's repeated flashes.
   - `gapAhead` (seconds, a positive number) shows an AHEAD row when you are not leading. The core currently sends null.
   - Missing or invalid values fall back safely; bestLap/lastLap of null, 0 or Infinity show as dim dashes.
11. **showCountdown:** values 3, 2, 1 or 'GO' (also 'GO!' or 0). Calling it again with the same value is ignored, so calling it every frame is safe. Each number stays on screen until the next value or hideCountdown().
12. **Message clearing:** showResults() and showMenu() clear any centre messages so they don't show blurred behind the screen. Flash messages live outside the race HUD layer, so intro messages are visible even while the race HUD is hidden.
13. **Bench imports:** dev/hud.html loads `createTrackPath` from src/world/track.js for real minimap data (read-only) and falls back to its own demo loop if that import fails.
known_issues: Fonts come from Google Fonts over the network. Offline, the HUD falls back to DIN Condensed / Arial Narrow / Roboto Condensed (looks fine, but less distinctive). Canvases redraw automatically once the fonts load.
Russo One has no italic, so the slant on the position number, countdown, logo, PAUSED and RESULTS comes from a CSS skew rather than a true italic.

Once, under heavy GPU load from several agents' headless Chrome sessions, a screenshot showed the tach and minimap blank (likely the browser wiping its 2D canvases). I added handlers so they redraw themselves; I could not reproduce it again.
When a screen is shown the root reads layout once to restart its intro animation (menu and results only, never during racing).

Not from the HUD: the real game's console logs many WebGL warnings: 'GL_INVALID_OPERATION: glDrawElements: Mismatch between texture format and sampler type (signed/unsigned/float/shadow)'. It probably comes from a shadow or depth texture in the world or post-processing code being sampled the wrong way. The integrator should pass this to the world/fx owners.
The countdown is centred and lifted 11% of screen height; in the chase camera it sits just above the car's roof, which is intentional for a countdown.
The bench page waits for the world's track module before it creates the HUD. With very short screenshot waits (around 1.2 s) under heavy load, the HUD may not exist yet; use --wait 3000 or more.
structured_report.perf_notes:
- **CPU cost:** measured live in the bench at 1080p, update() takes about 0.2 ms per frame including both canvas redraws, with about 2.3 DOM text changes per frame (lap time, total time, speed).
- **No layout thrash:** update() never reads layout; canvas sizes come from a ResizeObserver plus a resize listener for screen-density changes. Text is only written when the formatted string changes. Pop and flash effects use the Web Animations API (transform, colour, filter) without class tricks that force layout. Containers are style/layout-contained to limit restyles.
- **Tachometer:** a 25em square (400×400 at 1080p and density 1; density is capped at 2). Per frame: clear, two cached background images, two arc strokes, the nitro segments, and a needle with one small glow. The whole redraw is skipped when the needle moved less than 3 rpm, nitro is unchanged, and no shift or nitro effect is running. The background layers are rebuilt only on resize, font load, max-rpm change or canvas restore.
- **Minimap:** a 16.5em square. Per frame: about 35 grid lines in one stroke, the 256-point track path stroked four times (no blur filters), up to 7 dots, the arrow with one small glow, and the N label.
- **Blur:** during racing the only blurred-backdrop element is the small minimap (6px). The full-screen blur is used only on pause and results, when the game is paused or finished.
- **Idle cost:** while the race HUD is hidden (menu, intro), update() returns right away. Gamepad polling runs only while a menu screen is visible. No timers run per frame; messages use setTimeout.
- **Real game:** in the autopilot race with the HUD on, the game reported 60 fps and 61 draw calls (the HUD adds none to the 3D scene).
